title: Saffron and Orange Aioli
description: A short orange infusion draws the color and aroma from saffron before it is folded into a mellow garlic aioli.

ingredients.name: plain full-fat mayonnaise
ingredients.note: Use plain commercial mayonnaise made with pasteurized eggs.

ingredients.name: finely grated orange zest
ingredients.note: Colored peel only, grated to a paste.

steps.title: Infuse the orange juice
steps.text: Combine {orange}, {water}, {saffron} and {garlic} in a small covered saucepan. Simmer very gently for 5–7 minutes until the sliced garlic mashes with a fork.

steps.title: Mash and cool
steps.text: Mash the garlic and saffron into the liquid with the back of a spoon. Spread the mixture on a small plate and chill about 10 minutes until cold.

steps.title: Fold in the saffron
steps.text: Whisk the cooled infusion and {zest} into {mayo} until evenly colored.

steps.title: Adjust the consistency
steps.text: Scrape all of the mixture into the measuring cup. Add cold water a teaspoon at a time if needed to reach about 1 cup, maintaining a smooth spoonable texture.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Chill for 15 minutes to let the saffron develop, then serve a measured spoonful with steamed halibut or soft potatoes.

notes: Yield: About 1 cup. One serving is 2 tablespoons. Make ahead: Make the infusion a day ahead or chill the finished aioli for at least 15 minutes before using. Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The mayonnaise emulsion can separate as it thaws. Fridge reheat: Serve chilled. Stir until smooth just before portioning. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw covered in the refrigerator, then whisk or blend briefly and serve cold. Option A includes orange juice and zest. For gentler Option B, steep the saffron and garlic in water and omit the zest. The aioli is dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/8 of recipe): 155 kcal, 0.3 g protein, 0.7 g total carbohydrate, 16.8 g fat, 0.0 g fiber, 143 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
